page: Vultr vhp-8c-16gb-amd is a compute-focused instance within Vultr's High Performance family, built on the x86_64 architecture using AMD EPYC processors. The virtual machine provides 8 shared vCPUs across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, supporting standard instruction sets including AVX, AES-NI, and SHA extensions, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX instructions.

System memory consists of 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes bundled with 350 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs included on this server configuration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng tests, landing in the top 25 percent of instances. Multi-core compute benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core at 5,735 points, reflect average output aligned with shared-core allocation. Storage and memory benchmarks indicate solid middle-tier throughput, achieving 13.03 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.47 GB/s in static web serving. Natural language processing and larger model inference show limitations, as seen in weak scores for 7B LLM prompt processing.

Balancing an 8-vCPU configuration with 350 GB of fast local NVMe storage without dedicated CPU pricing premiums delivers cost efficiency for multi-threaded tasks that do not require massive per-core memory. Vultr vhp-8c-16gb-amd is suited for software build pipelines, static and dynamic web serving, cache nodes, and continuous integration workflows.
description: Vultr vhp-8c-16gb-amd is a compute-oriented virtual server configured with 8 shared vCPUs across 4 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz on x86_64 architecture. It provides 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 resource allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware setup includes 350 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a public IPv4 address, without GPU acceleration. Synthetic benchmarks reflect top-tier single-core compute stress performance paired with mid-range multi-core scores, software compilation speeds, and Redis key-value throughput. The lack of AVX-512 and modest memory per core limits heavy matrix calculations and massive in-memory databases, but the bundled fast NVMe storage provides solid resource density. This server fits build automation pipelines, continuous integration systems, web application hosting, and middle-tier database operations.
